## Interpreting the sign of the scalar product {#iv5-angle-exploration .vector-lesson .magnitude-lesson .geometric-lesson}

Change the angle and lengths. What makes the result **positive, zero or negative**?

<div data-geometric="explore"></div>

::: notes
The result is always visible as a·b=value, without a substituted calculation or a separate list of vector values. The labelled diagram shows the angle; the controls change θ and both positive magnitudes. Start at |a|=2, |b|=5, θ=60°. Ask students to vary lengths at a fixed angle: the size changes but the sign does not. At 90° the value is exactly zero for any positive lengths. Compare 0° with an acute angle, and 180° with an obtuse angle: positive does not necessarily mean same direction and negative does not necessarily mean opposite directions. Presets 0°,90°,180° and Reset support these comparisons. Reset restores 2,5,60°. No 3D interactive.
:::
